sentences.text: Orophosaurus is considered a dubious genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in New Mexico.
This animal belongs to the family Elasmosauridae and the order Plesiosauria.
The genus is known only from its type species, O. pauciporus, based on fossil specimen AMNH 5692.
This holotype was found in the Late Cretaceous Fox Hills Formation within the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.
The specimen consists of portions of three cervical vertebrae.
In 1962, Welles judged Orophosaurus to be a nomen vanum due to the very fragmentary nature of its holotype.
The only known species of Orophosaurus is Orophosaurus pauciporus, which serves as the type species designated for the genus.
